defects.justification: Forwarded events are re-signed with the provider's WEBHOOK_SECRET, so every merchant must hold that secret to verify callbacks, and any merchant can then forge signed provider events (e.g. fake payment.succeeded) to this receiver. Use a separate per-merchant signing key.
The full request body is read into memory before the signature is checked and there is no size limit, so an unauthenticated client can send huge bodies to exhaust memory.
The merchant events listing is guarded by one global API token, so whoever holds it can read every merchant's payment events by changing merchant_id; there is no per-merchant authorization.

Signature covers only the body and there is no timestamp/nonce tolerance window; de-duplication by event id blunts exact replays, but captured signed events are valid forever (README admits no replay protection).

Forwarding of successful payments is a single attempt: a timeout or 5xx just marks the row 'failed', and a crash after insert leaves it 'pending' forever, so merchants silently miss payment notifications with no retry or re-drive.
hmac.compare_digest raises TypeError when given a str with non-ASCII characters, so an unauthenticated request with a non-ASCII X-Signature header produces a 500 instead of 401.
json.loads accepts UTF-16/UTF-32 bodies but body.decode() assumes UTF-8, so a validly signed non-UTF-8 JSON event raises UnicodeDecodeError and returns 500 (provider will keep redelivering).
fastapi, uvicorn, httpx and pytest are completely unpinned, so builds are non-reproducible and exposed to breaking or malicious releases.
